'''Philip Douglas  Lawley''' (4 July 1927 – 18 December 2011)<ref name="natureobit">{{Cite journal | last1 = Venitt | first1 = Stanley| last2 = Phillips | first2 = David H. | doi = 10.1038/482036a | title = Philip D. Lawley (1927–2011) Chemist who discovered that cancer is caused by damage to DNA.| journal = Nature | volume = 482 | issue = 7383 | pages = 36 | year = 2012 | pmid =  22297963| doi-access = free }}</ref> was a British [[chemist]], best known for demonstrating that DNA damage was the base cause of cancer working with Peter Brookes.<ref name="natureobit"/><ref name="icrpressrelease">{{cite web|url=http://www.icr.ac.uk/press/recent_featured_articles/Professor%20Philip%20Lawley_Obituary/index.shtml|title=Professor Philip Lawley|archive-date=2012-03-10|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120310182659/http://www.icr.ac.uk/press/recent_featured_articles/Professor%20Philip%20Lawley_Obituary/index.shtml|url-status=dead}}</ref> In January 2003 the ICR honoured the achievements of Brookes and Lawley by naming a £21m laboratory after them. It is devoted to research on the genetic nature of cancer and located next to the Haddow laboratories.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Venitt|first=Stanley|date=2012-01-23|title=Philip Lawley obituary|url=http://www.theguardian.com/science/2012/jan/23/philip-lawley|access-date=2020-08-04|website=The Guardian|language=en}}</ref>
